text:
mira: quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide which long-term refactor to land for the continuous-batcher scheduler. TL;DR: two paths (soft-reserve lanes vs strict lane isolation) and different eviction models.

eli: can you summarize the user-visible tradeoffs? deadlines, p99, and tail cost are what the SRE team cares about.

mira: short: soft-reserve lanes = better packing / lower cost for small requests but more tail variance under noise. strict isolation = predictable p99 at higher steady cost. also: preemptible microbatches affect kv-cache affinity.

sam: my worry with soft-reserve is runaway noisy tenants. We had that postmortem earlier — any mitigations baked into the design?

mira: yes — plan is: per-tenant "headroom tokens" that expire, admission window monitors, and a cheap circuit-breaker to force strict lane fallback. also a background rebalancer that moves tenants to dedicated lanes when sustained.

jordan: for implementation boundaries, can we keep the admission API simple? i'd like: enqueue(req), hint(deadline, token_count), cancel(id). Avoid exposing lanes to callers.

anu: agreed. also need a clear fastpath for tiny requests: if token_count <= 16 and lane==soft, do immediate microbatch with no prefetch. That reduced tail in the experiment.

mira: noted. RFC follow-up question: do we mandate lease heartbeats (every 100ms) from the runtime to track headroom, or store per-tenant counters in the allocator? tradeoffs: heartbeat increases control-plane traffic, counters complicate cross-gpu rebalancing.

eli: prefer heartbeat model + aggregator service. easier to reason about liveness and eviction signals. we can compress heartbeats and sample.

sam: +1 for heartbeat. but add an escape hatch: admin override to pin a tenant to strict lanes for incidents.

jordan: operational notes: telemetry we need out of the batched path: per-lane p50/p95/p99, microbatch size histogram, preempt rates, and kv-cache hit ratio per-tenant. without those we can't tune quantization/batching tradeoffs.

mira: agreed. i'll add concrete observability fields to the rollout checklist.

infra-bot: deploy check: canary on 2 nodes with soft-reserve enabled, fallback window=250ms, heartbeat interval=100ms.

anu: one more design nit — eviction hysteresis. please include a cooldown so we don't thrash tenant placement when transient spikes occur.

mira: yes: cooldown = max(1s, 3x tenant p95). i'll write the follow-up doc with configs and a short compatibility shim for older clients that call enqueue(...) with no deadline hint.

eli: thanks — look forward to the doc. if we go heartbeat+aggregator, i'll prototype the compressed heartbeat protobuf.

mira: ok i'll drop a draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
